sn20.7:1.2: Probably the people known in Sanskrit as the Daśārṇa of the western Vindhya mountains. | The _mudiṅga_ is a doubled-headed drum known today as _mridangam_, which is still widely used in southern India. It is named for the paste (“mud”) applied to one of the heads that gives it its distinctive snare tone. The head is attached with a wooden rim that is tightened with leather straps. | _Āṇaka_ is another name for what is said to be a large military drum. The context here suggests that the original sense was “pegged”, in reference to the pegs used under the leather straps for tuning.
sn20.7:1.4: Puskara is another kind of drum, identified with the mudinga
